## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

content.text:
So an index.html static project is expected. The game should be a single-page static site (probably with JS modules). The task: "2D Fortnite building inside a Worms artillery match" — build a browser game combining Worms-style turn-based artillery with Fortnite-style building (place blocks/ramps/walls quickly, maybe mats from destroyed terrain).

I should design and build a polished, playable game. Key features:
- 2D destructible terrain (pixel/heightmap or tile grid).
- Turn-based artillery: select angle/power, fire projectile, wind, damage, knockback.
- Fortnite building: place wood/brick/metal walls, floors, ramps, using harvested materials. Building is grid-based (Fortnite-style tiles) with fast placement (click+drag or hotkeys). Structures have HP, can be destroyed by explosions.
- Mobile touch support (Agents.md requires responsive + touch controls).
- Local 2-player (hotseat) vs AI.
- Visual polish: cartoon style, particles, screen shake, sound (WebAudio synth), UI.

Should I use Canvas 2D. Single index.html + maybe modules. Keep it self-contained, no dependencies (avoid npm). Use HTML file with CSS and JS split into files? Simpler: index.html, style.css, game.js. Static server serves.

Need to check screenshot capture process. playwright-cli available. I'll build, run server, screenshot, inspect.

Let me think carefully about the game design and implementation details to make it genuinely fun and coherent.

Title: "WORMS: BUILD ROYALE" or "Trench Royale". Tagline: "Worms-style artillery. Fortnite-style building."

Game design:

Battlefield: 1600x900 logical world, canvas scaled to fit. Terrain generated with layered noise, destructible. Two (or more?) teams of worms. Let's do 1v1 (player vs AI) and maybe 2-player local toggle. Each team has 2 worms? Worms matches typically 4 worms per team. Complexity: switching worms after turn. Could do 2 worms per team, health 100 each, with worm icons. Keep it manageable but rich.

Actually, to focus on building mechanic, 1 worm per side with 100 HP is fine, but Fortnite building needs mats. Could add 3 worms per team; active worm switches each turn; dead worms removed. AI needs to handle building too — simple: AI sometimes builds a wall/roof when low HP or after taking damage.

Mechanics:
- Turn: active worm. Move with A/D (limited move points per turn, e.g., 90px), jump (W/Space), aim with mouse or arrow keys, hold to charge power? Worms uses power meter. Fortnite building needs quick inputs. Let's design:
  - Move: A/D, jump: W or Space.
  - Aim: mouse position; angle indicator line. Fire: hold left mouse on battlefield? Conflict with building. Better: 
    - Aim via mouse, click+drag to set power, release to fire (classic).
    - Build mode toggled with B or right-click? Build palette: keys 1-4 (wall, floor, ramp, roof?) and left-click places. Fortnite building is about quick wall-ramp-floor. We can have build hotkeys: Q = wall, E = ramp, F = floor, and click places at cursor snapped to build grid. Right-click cancels.
  - On mobile: on-screen controls: move left/right, jump, aim joystick + fire button, build buttons.

Simplify: aim with mouse; press/hold left mouse button on empty space to charge power (arc preview), release fire. In build mode (toggle B or hold Q/E/F?) placement is click. Maybe cleaner: a mode switch "COMBAT / BUILD". In combat, drag to aim. In build, click to place selected piece. Keyboard shortcuts Q (wall), E (ramp), C (floor) instantly switch to build mode with that piece selected; B toggles. Right click / Esc back to combat.

Mats: wood 0 start? Give 60 wood, 40 brick, 20 metal? Fortnite harvesting: destroying terrain/structures with explosions yields mats. Also each turn passive +? Give starting 100 wood, 50 brick, 30 metal. Walls cost 10 wood, ramps 10, floors 10? Different mat types cost differently: wood 10, brick 20, metal 30, with increasing HP. Selecting material with keys? Could be overkill. Alternative: build pieces always cost "wood" and materials are upgraded by harvest? Hmm.

Let's make material selection: keys 1/2/3 choose Wood/Brick/Metal, costs 10/15/25. Pieces: Wall (Q), Ramp (E), Floor (F). Each piece HP scales by material (wood 60, brick 120, metal 200). Structures are grid-aligned 40px cells, with orientation. Ramps occupy a cell as a diagonal triangle (collision approximated?). This gets complicated for collision with worms/projectiles. Need a reasonable model.

Implementation approach for terrain and structures:

Use a tile grid for terrain: cell size 16px? World 1600x900 => 100x56 cells. Terrain destructible with circular carve. Collision: heightmap would be simpler for terrain but building needs grid. Tile grid works: solidity per cell. Explosion carves circle by clearing cells. Rendering terrain: draw each cell with grass top detection, or use offscreen canvas for terrain texture and mask. For visual quality, use offscreen terrain canvas drawn with noisy surface and carve via destination-out. But collision needs a mask. Use grid of booleans for collision and draw terrain to offscreen at cell resolution then upscale? Could draw a smooth filled path of heightmap for visuals and use grid for collision. Mismatch acceptable if aligned.

Better: heightmap terrain (array width columns, surface y). Destructible craters via carving a radial hole into heightmap? Explosions on side of hills should carve caves; heightmap only supports top-down erosion. Worms-like terrain is fully destructible with caves. Use pixel bitmask at low res (e.g., 4px) and render upscaled with smoothing; collision sampling. World 1600x900 at 4px => 400x225 = 90k booleans, fine. Draw terrain into offscreen canvas 400x225 then scale up with imageSmoothing maybe false for chunky look. Carve circles on offscreen and update mask. For nicer look, draw noise layers/grass on top via per-column surface detection from mask. Could render terrain each frame from mask into an ImageData at 400x225 with colors computed per pixel (dirt gradient + grass based on whether above is empty). That's 90k pixels per frame — okay but expensive-ish; only re-render on destruction, cached.

Alternatively canvas polygon silhouette from heightmap plus caves. Let's do mask + cached offscreen render on destruction, scaled with smoothing for a soft cartoon look? Pixelated at 4px scale looks blocky; could use 2px => 800x450 = 360k pixels, fine for occasional re-render. Render at 2px, scale 2x. Use ImageData color computation: for each solid pixel, determine depth below surface (distance to nearest air above) → top 6px grass green, then dirt brown gradient with noise. Air pixels transparent. That gives nice terrain with grass edges following craters? Crater interiors would be brown/dark depending depth. Distance-to-air-above for grass only: grass appears at tops of overhangs too? Using check if pixel above is air → grass edge. For cave ceilings, pixel above is solid so no grass. Good.

Terrain generation: multi-octave sine noise heightmap, base ground y ~ 620. Add hills. Also floating islands? For building fun maybe add some platform terrain. Keep one big landscape with hills and a valley. Maybe add a small floating island in middle? Structures stand on terrain. Could make center pit. Let's generate two mounds with valley; worms spawn on each mound.

Collision: worms as circles radius 9. Ground collision: sample mask; move worm step by step; when feet hit solid, stop. Need robust walking on slopes: try moving horizontally, then push up if embedded, and gravity.

Worm physics:
- position, velocity, onGround, facing.
- Each turn move budget (e.g., 100 px). Move with accel; step up small ledges by snapping up when blocked (up to 8px).
- Jump: vy = -something. Limited? unlimited jumping okay but move budget prevents travel. Also jumping costs a bit of move budget.
- Falling damage? Maybe small. Keep.

Aiming:
- Active worm has aim angle (relative to facing? absolute 0-360) and power 0-100. Mouse aim: angle from worm to mouse, power set by drag distance? Classic Worms: hold mouse to charge power bar oscillating or increasing; release to fire. Let's implement: press and hold left mouse → power charges 0→100 over ~1.2s then stays? Oscillates? For precision, drag: power proportional to drag distance from press point. That's intuitive and works on touch. Arc preview shown dotted (with gravity/wind). Release fires.
- Keyboard: arrows adjust angle, up/down power? Maybe not necessary but add.

Weapons: Bazooka (infinite), Grenade (3 per worm, bounces, 3s fuse), maybe "Build Blaster"? Keep 2 weapons plus "harvest" mechanic. Keys 1 bazooka, 2 grenade. But keys also used for materials; put materials on 7/8/9? Let's define controls cleanly:

Combat:
- Mouse: aim; press-drag-release to set power and fire.
- 1/2: select Bazooka/Grenade.
- A/D move, Space jump.
- Q/E/F: build wall/ramp/floor (enters build mode)
- B: toggle build mode.
- Tab? no.

Build mode:
- Left click place selected piece at snapped grid (within range of active worm, e.g., 220px).
- 1/2/3 select Wood/Brick/Metal.
- Q/E/F select Wall/Ramp/Floor.
- Right-click/Esc/B exit.
- Buildings cost mats; destroyed structures drop mats (for both? whoever's turn). Explosions harvest mats into active player's pool if within radius? Fortnite-like: you farm by destroying. Give mats on destruction to the shooter/owner of the turn.

Build pieces & collision:
- Grid cell size 48. Wall: full cell vertical rectangle (thin? Fortnite wall occupies a tile). Simpler: Wall = solid 48x48 block (but visually a wall with border, maybe 12px thick centered?). For collision with projectiles, full block is easiest. But blocky walls everywhere may look ugly; stylized wooden panels are fine.
- Floor: horizontal platform 48x12 at bottom or top of cell; collision as thin rect.
- Ramp: triangle from bottom-left to top-right (or oriented toward cursor?). Collision with triangle; projectile collision complex. Could treat ramp as a set of 4 horizontal strips forming a staircase approximation. Implement ramp as triangle path with 6 stair strips for collision and draw as triangle with wooden planks. Simpler and robust: ramp is a diagonal set of small rects. Player can walk up (step height snapping). 

Alternatively, make all build pieces full blocks but ramps drawn diagonally — collision approximate full block would block movement, bad.

Let me implement structures as objects with type and cell coords and a list of collision rects:
- wall: rect (x, y, w, h) maybe 48x48 but visually panel with slight inset; also orientation? vertical wall.
- floor: rect (x, y, 48, 14) at cell bottom? Place based on cursor cell; draw platform.
- ramp: 6 stair rects from bottom to top; visually a filled triangle with plank lines; collision with stair rects.

Placement validity: cell must not overlap terrain? Fortnite pieces can be placed on terrain. Allow placement if cell's area mostly air; wall placed on ground will intersect terrain — that's okay visually? Wall in air adjacent to ground is useful. Allow anywhere within range if not overlapping an existing structure; snap to grid. Maybe restrict wall cell center within 260px of worm. Also to make building meaningful, allow placing while projectile incoming? Turn-based so building happens on your turn; AI can build on its turn. Fortnite tension comes from building under fire, but turn-based can't replicate live. Could add "reaction building": after firing, opponent gets a brief window to build a defensive wall? Hmm, that's a neat twist: When a projectile is in flight, the defender can spend mats to build instantly (reaction build) with limited time? That complicates. Maybe simpler: during the opponent's projectile flight, you can place one emergency wall at a cost (reaction build), triggered with a button/click. Actually this is the key fusion of Fortnite: building in response to incoming fire. Let's implement "REACTION BUILD": while a projectile is airborne and heading toward you, a small timer/charge lets you click/tap to instantly build a wall in front of your active worm (costs 15 wood/brick/metal), once per enemy shot. The wall can block the shot. This is a great mechanic and distinguishes the game.

Implementation: after firing, projectile flight; defender (the player not firing) can press Space or click "BUILD!" button to erect a wall between their worm and incoming projectile, if within range and mats. Place automatically at a position ~60px from worm toward projectile, snapped, if space free. Limit one reaction build per incoming shot, costs mats. AI defender does it with probability based on difficulty/threat.

This is compelling. Need clear UI prompt when projectile in flight: "INCOMING — TAP TO BUILD (15 wood)". Reaction window maybe only until projectile within 300px, or anytime during flight with cooldown. One per shot.

Damage:
- Bazooka explosion radius 55, damage up to 45 at center falloff; knockback.
- Grenade: bounces, 2.5s fuse, radius 65, damage 55.
- Worm HP 100. Two worms per team? With reaction building and building, 1v1 might be quick. Let's do 3 worms per team? AI complexity for switching and movement. Hotseat local and vs AI.

Let's do teams of 2 worms each: "Blue" (you) and "Red" (AI). Active worm alternates teams each turn; within a team, the next alive worm becomes active. Health 100 each. Win when all enemy worms dead. This makes matches longer and lets you use building more.

AI:
- On its turn: evaluate. Simple AI: choose weapon; aim at nearest enemy worm with ballistic solve (iterate angle/power with gravity+wind simulation), account for obstacles? Use a search: sample angles 20-80 and powers 40-100, simulate trajectory with collision against terrain/structures, score landing proximity to target; pick best (with randomness). Then fire. Occasionally (30%) build a defensive wall/ramp near itself if low HP or after being hit, using mats. Also reaction build with probability when incoming.
- AI turn timing: think 0.8s, aim preview, fire. Use async state machine with timers. Could make AI build first then fire, or fire then build? Worms turn: either move/shoot. Let's allow AI to build a wall then shoot with reduced power? Building doesn't consume turn except movement? In our game, building is free actions during your turn (limited by mats and placement range), then you fire to end turn. That's fine. Player can build multiple pieces then fire. Good.

Turn flow:
1. Turn starts for team. Select worm. Movement budget reset. Camera focuses worm.
2. Player can move, build, aim/fire. Firing ends turn (after projectile resolves and damage settles).
3. After shot resolution, switch to other team. Wind changes slightly each turn.
4. Reaction build window during projectile flight for the defending team (human or AI).

If player doesn't fire, no turn timer? Add optional turn timer (45s) to keep pace? Could show "NO TIMER" casual. Maybe a soft timer that auto-fires? Skip.

Movement: A/D. Movement budget 80px per turn displayed. Jump costs 5. Building doesn't cost budget but mats. This makes positioning matter.

Camera: world 1600x900 might fit 16:9 screens fully; on mobile portrait it needs scaling/cropping. Could make world 1440x810 and scale to fit, showing whole battlefield — simpler and good for aiming. On mobile portrait, letterboxed with controls below. Responsive: canvas fits width/height with aspect ratio; world 1440x810. Entire battlefield visible makes aiming and building easy. Yes, no camera scrolling. Worms matches typically side-scrolling but full view is fine for a compact match. Use 1440x810.

Actually on phones, 1440x810 scaled to 390px wide → tiny worms. Mobile UX requires zoom/pan or larger world scale. Alternative: canvas fill screen with camera following active worm and aim. More complex. Could do CSS: on portrait, canvas fills width, height = width*9/16 (~219px), leaving huge empty space; controls below. Game small but playable? Worms would be ~7px. Not great.

Better responsive approach: render with camera that scales to fit a "safe" view of width ~900 world px, following action. But then building/aiming across map needs panning. Worms games scroll. We can implement camera: view width = min(world width, 900) on desktop; mobile view width ~600 world units, camera follows active worm / projectile, with smooth panning. Add auto-zoom based on aspect. Aiming with mouse/touch relative to world coordinates via transform. Mini-map indicator showing enemies. This is more work but doable.

Maybe keep it simpler: world 1600x900; camera viewport aspect matches canvas; desktop shows ~1600 width (whole map) if canvas 16:9. On mobile landscape (common for games), whole map still fits width, tiny but landscape phone ~800px wide gives decent. Portrait: show controls and rotate suggestion overlay "Rotate for best experience" but still playable with camera zoom. Hmm.

Agents.md mandates mobile support. Let's implement camera with zoom to fit world height and view width = min(worldW, viewH*aspect...). Actually:
- Fit world height to canvas height, so scale = canvasH / 900. View width in world = canvasW / scale. On 16:9 canvas, view width = 1600 (world width 1600) — whole map. On portrait canvas 390x600, scale=600/900=0.667, view width=585 world px — zoomed in. Camera follows active worm/projectile. On landscape phone 800x360, scale=0.4, view=2000 > 1600, show whole map with letterbox. Good.
- Clamp camera x between 0 and worldW - viewW. Camera follows active worm when idle; follows projectile in flight; returns to active worm after.
- Touch aim: drag from worm? Tap-and-drag anywhere: angle/power based on vector from worm to touch point; drag distance controls power. Fire button separate? On touch, tap sets aim, then press "FIRE" button to shoot using power slider? Could be confusing. Simpler touch: drag anywhere on canvas → shows aim; release fires immediately. But building needs tap to place. In build mode tap places. Reaction build tap button. Good.
- But on mobile, tapping to aim/fire could accidentally fire when trying to just look. Camera auto-follows; no manual panning needed. Fine.

Desktop mouse: aiming line follows mouse; hold left button to charge? Let's do drag-to-fire: press at any point, drag sets angle & power (power from distance capped 400px => 100), release fires. Also show aim line on hover with current power? Standard approach: aim angle from worm to cursor; power via drag distance. Actually if press point is arbitrary, angle should be from worm to current cursor, not drag vector. Power from distance of cursor from worm? Then just click far = max power, click near = low. That's intuitive: aim at target, distance = power. But precision limited. Alternative power meter: hold mouse button, power oscillates 0→100 over 1.5s, click again to fire. Worms classic uses hold to charge. For a snappy game, drag from worm like Angry Birds is best: press near worm, drag opposite to set angle/power (slingshot) — very intuitive. But then aiming across map with camera? Hmm.

Let's use: hover mouse shows aim direction from active worm to cursor; power controlled by holding left mouse button — a power bar fills 0→100 in 1.1s and oscillates back and forth? Release to fire. This is classic Worms-ish and precise enough (you time the bar). But harder with mouse than drag. Many artillery games (Shellshock) use drag. 

I think "drag from worm" slingshot is excellent for touch and mouse: pointer down near/anywhere → anchor at worm; drag away; vector from pointer to worm defines launch direction and power; dotted arc preview updates; release fires. This is like Angry Birds. But to aim at something on the other side, you drag opposite — initially unintuitive but standard. Alternatively drag toward target with power = distance, launch in that direction — also intuitive (like pulling a bow? no). Use "drag toward target, distance = power" with power curve: launch toward pointer, power = clamp(dist/500). Then you can point at enemy and pull farther for more power. Simple and direct. Arc preview shows. Let's do that. On release, if power < 8%, cancel (avoid accidental). Show power percent.

But then clicking to aim without firing isn't possible. Fine.

Keyboard fallback: arrows adjust angle (Left/Right), Up/Down power, Space fire? Space is jump. Use Enter to fire. Provide instructions in help modal. Not crucial.

HUD:
- Top center: turn indicator, wind gauge with arrows, round timer? 
- Top left: Blue team worms with HP bars and active highlight; top right: Red team.
- Bottom left: active worm portrait + HP + ammo; bottom center: mats (wood/brick/metal counts) + build palette; bottom right: weapon selector.
- Build mode overlay: grid ghost preview, cost, validity color, "BUILD MODE" banner.
- Incoming prompt: big pulsing "⚠ INCOMING — CLICK / TAP TO BUILD" button at bottom center.
- Event feed / floating combat text (damage numbers, "BLOCKED!", "MATS +10").
- Help button (?) with controls; start screen with title, mode select (1P vs AI / 2P local), maybe difficulty.

Visual style:
- Cartoon vector: sky gradient with sun, parallax clouds, distant hills, grass terrain with flowers/rocks; worms as cute pink/blue grubs with helmets; structures wooden planks with nails, brick with mortar, metal with rivets; explosions with particles and smoke; screen shake; hit flash; slow-mo on final kill? 
- Sound: WebAudio synth for shoot, explosion, build, click, damage, victory jingle. Toggle mute.
- Background music? Simple ambient loop with oscillators might be annoying; maybe light rhythmic bass? Skip music or add subtle. Sound effects only.

Tech: Plain HTML/CSS/JS. Split files: index.html, styles.css, js/game.js maybe modules. Static server supports modules. Keep game.js ~2000 lines? That's fine. Maybe split into modules for maintainability: engine (terrain, physics), game logic, render, audio, ui. Given single-file simpler for debugging? I'll split: 
- index.html
- styles.css
- src/main.js (boot/UI wiring)
- src/terrain.js
- src/audio.js
- src/ai.js
- src/game.js (state machine, physics)
- src/render.js
- src/input.js? 

Could be cleaner with fewer files: game.js containing everything except audio. But large. Let's do modules.

Actually, tools allow creating files. I need to be careful about correctness. A single big JS file might be easier to keep consistent. But 2500 lines in one file is okay. I'll do:
- index.html (markup + UI)
- styles.css
- src/terrain.js (Terrain class: mask, generate, carve, collide, render cache)
- src/audio.js (SFX)
- src/ai.js (AI aim solver)
- src/game.js (core game, entities, input, render, loop)
- src/ui.js? HUD updates inline in game.js.

Let's plan details deeply before coding.

World:
- W=1600, H=900. Terrain ground base y ~ 640. Sky above.
- Terrain mask resolution: 2px cells => 800x450. Use Uint8Array. Collision sample via mask at world coords. Render terrain to offscreen canvas 800x450, scaled 2x with smoothing? If using imageSmoothingEnabled=true when drawing upscaled, edges blur. Use false for crisp pixel style; at 2px scale it's subtle. Could render at 1px resolution for smooth-ish edges: 1600x900 ImageData = 1.44M pixels, re-render only on carve (each explosion) — acceptable maybe ~20ms. Carving also updates 1.44M mask? Explosion carving loops bounding box only. Rendering full 1.44M pixel color computation per explosion could cause hitch (few ms to 20ms). Let's use 2px mask (800x450=360k) for both collision and render; render at 800x450 and upscale 2x with smoothing disabled. Chunky retro look consistent with cartoon? Slight pixelation at 2x is fine and stylized. Maybe apply smoothing for soft edges? Test visually.

Terrain generation:
- Use seeded value noise 1D for surface height: h(x) = base + sum of sines with random phases. Add plateau-ish hills. Need spawn areas relatively flat at x ~ 220 and ~ 1380.

## Objective
- Build a polished, playable browser game combining Worms-style 2D turn-based artillery with Fortnite-style building, based on the user prompt: "2D Fortnite building inside a Worms artillery match".

## Requirements
- User gave only the game concept; no explicit additional requirements.
- Implied by repo conventions: responsive desktop/mobile browser game with usable touch controls.
- Must be a static site served by `start.sh` (existing runtime expects `index.html` or a Vite project).

## Decisions
- Built a dependency-free static HTML/CSS/JS game (no npm framework) so the existing static server works.
- World: `1280x720`, destructible pixel-mask terrain, two teams of two worms, hotseat/CPU modes, turn-based artillery.
- Fortnite mechanics: wood/brick/metal materials, wall/ramp/floor grid building, build range, material farming from destroyed terrain/builds, loot crates, and a unique reaction-build during incoming projectiles.
- Weapons: bazooka (infinite) and grenade (3 per worm, bounces, fuse).
- CPU AI samples ballistic trajectories with difficulty-scaled error and sometimes builds/reaction-builds.
- Audio synthesized via WebAudio; no external assets.
- Chose a full-map camera on desktop and a follow/midpoint camera with edge markers on portrait.
- Menu uses a live battlefield behind the title overlay; game starts only after mode selection.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html` with menu, HUD, help, game-over overlay, reaction banner, touch controls, and inline favicon.
- Created `styles.css` with full responsive styling, HUD panels, build/reaction UI, overlays, animations, and mobile breakpoints.
- Created `src/terrain.js`: destructible terrain generation, caves, floating island, carving, surface/top tracking, flood-filled dark caves, rendered offscreen terrain, grass tufts.
- Created `src/physics.js`: gravity/wind constants, weapons, projectile speed, collision helpers, blast line-of-sight test, trajectory simulation.
- Created `src/audio.js`: WebAudio SFX for shoot/explosion/build/jump/hit/death/win/reaction/etc., mute persistence.
- Created `src/ai.js`: trajectory-sampling CPU shot planner with difficulty settings.
- Created `src/render.js`: full canvas renderer for sky, sun, clouds, hills, terrain, caves, structures, crates, worms, aim preview, build ghost, projectiles, particles, floating text, edge markers, vignette.
- Created `src/hud.js`: DOM HUD generation/update, team panels, wind gauge, weapon/material/piece dock, reaction banner, hints, toasts.
- Created `src/game.js`: game state machine, turn flow, movement/jumping, aiming/firing, building, reaction building, explosions, damage, materials, AI turns/reactions, camera, input, update/render loop, menu/help/game-over wiring.
- Verified all JS files parse with `node --input-type=module --check`.
- Started server on port `3002` in tmux session `game`; confirmed HTTP 200.
- Installed missing Playwright Chromium `chromium-1243`; captured menu and gameplay screenshots.
- Fixed terrain caves rendering as light green by adding flood-fill dark cave rendering; thickened floating island.
- Fixed initial aim preview clutter by only drawing the aim arc while actively aiming.
- Added inline favicon to remove 404 console errors.
- Screenshots inspected: menu looks polished; gameplay scene works, HUD readable, terrain and worms render.

### Active
- Browser testing of actual gameplay interactions (aim/fire, building, AI turns, reaction build, mobile layout).
- Need to lighten the menu overlay further; current menu still looks quite dark.
- Need to verify drag-to-aim/fire and build placement via Playwright mouse commands.
- Need to check mobile portrait and landscape layouts with screenshots.
- Need to remove temporary debug hook `window.__trench = state` or keep only if useful.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Use Playwright mouse commands to drag from the active worm toward the enemy, release, and verify projectile flight/explosion/turn switching.
2. Test build mode: press `Q`, click grid cells, verify wall placement, material deduction, and HUD updates.
3. Test reaction build during an incoming projectile, both human and CPU.
4. Test local 2P mode and CPU AI turns through several rounds.
5. Capture desktop, tablet landscape, and phone portrait screenshots; fix layout/camera issues.
6. Lighten menu overlay so the battlefield is more visible; reduce the dark radial/linear overlay.
7. Remove or gate `window.__trench` debug hook, then final smoke test and clean console.
8. Optionally improve central terrain shape if it still reads as an unnatural mesa after mobile/desktop inspection.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: page structure, HUD, overlays, controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: all visual styling and responsive behavior.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: core game logic, state, input, turn flow, building, explosions, AI, loop.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/render.js`: canvas rendering of world/entities/effects.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/terrain.js`: destructible terrain and cave rendering.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/physics.js`: projectile simulation and collision helpers.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/hud.js`: HUD DOM updates and dock buttons.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ai.js`: CPU shot selection.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: WebAudio sound effects.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: saved menu/game screenshots for visual review.
- `/tmp/opencode/server.log`: server log output.

## Important Context
- Dev server is running in tmux session `game` on `http://localhost:3002`; restart with `tmux kill-session -t game` then `PORT=3002 ./start.sh`.
- Playwright CLI requires `DISPLAY=:0` and config only on `open`:
  - `DISPLAY=:0 playwright-cli --config $HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json open http://localhost:3002`
  - Subsequent commands: `DISPLAY=:0 playwright-cli screenshot --filename screenshots/foo.png` (do not pass `--config`).
- Playwright window viewport is roughly `1049x788`; use `playwright-cli resize <w> <h>` to test other sizes.
- Server currently has only favicon 404s resolved; check console logs under `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/output/`.
- Temporary debug hook at end of `src/game.js`: `window.__trench = state;` allows evaluating terrain/game state from Playwright.
- Screenshot files: `screenshots/menu.png`, `menu2.png`, `game1.png`, `game2.png`.
- Menu overlay was lightened once but still appears dark; CSS `.menu-overlay` and `.menu-overlay::before` control this.
- `styles.css` has breakpoints at `1050px`, `820px`, `560px`, `pointer: coarse`, and landscape max-height `620px`.
- `AGENTS.md`/repo conventions were provided separately; do not repeat them in output.
